claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations can be used to study the thermal stability of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles as a function of size.
The thermal stability of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles decreases as nanoparticle size decreases.
The initial material consists of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles of various sizes.
Molecular dynamics simulations will be conducted to analyze thermal stability.
The simulations will vary temperature to assess thermal response as a function of nanoparticle size.
Atomic interactions and bonding characteristics within the nanoparticles mediate their thermal response.
Smaller nanoparticles have higher surface-to-volume ratios.
A higher surface-to-volume ratio leads to greater surface energy.
Greater surface energy reduces the thermal stability of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles will have lower thermal stability than larger FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
Larger FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles provide the thermal-stability baseline.
The proposed study is restricted to FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles and does not address other compositions or materials.
Prior theoretical study of the relationship between size and thermal stability in this system is limited.
The exact relationship between nanoparticle size and thermal stability is uncertain.
Thermal-stability profiles, phase-transition temperatures, and energy fluctuations will be measured in simulations of differently sized nanoparticles.
The hypothesis is falsified if smaller nanoparticles do not exhibit lower thermal stability than larger nanoparticles.
